tldr: Two pieces earn scout-credibility. Three are softer than their headlines.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Hand it to my pitching analytics group Monday morning. The bidirectional asymmetry — Q1 recovers, Q4 craters on both K% and FIP — matches what every veteran pro scout has been saying about sell-high windows for thirty years. The 'selling team knows something' framing is the most actionable sentence on the whole site.
articles.what_is_missing: Who is on the selling side of the Q4 trades? If TBR/CLE/LAD are concentrated as sellers, that's a buy-list, not generic mean reversion.
articles.honest_critique: Solid finding. Light on the human story of who's on the other side of the desk.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Reframes how I'd talk about trade evaluation in our front office — less time on FV ledger, more time on big-league acquisition selection and org-dev infrastructure.
articles.what_is_missing: Coaching/staff continuity as a covariate. The pitching coach, hitting coordinator, and Latin American academy director drive more of the 'org dev fit' effect than the GM does. Public information, not used.
articles.honest_critique: Best methodology of the five. The 'r=0.45 across 48 GMs' is exactly the kind of effect size I trust.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Nothing. The mechanism story — bilingual coaching, biomechanics infrastructure — is right, but the chart is screaming 'market size confound.'
articles.what_is_missing: Latin American academy director tenure. Latin scouting infrastructure investment by org. The actual mechanisms.
articles.honest_critique: The methodology callout admits the central confound is unchecked. Either run the check or don't publish.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Mild adjustment to package construction thinking. Doesn't reach the level of changing a deal in front of me.
articles.what_is_missing: Test against total acquired-WAR — breadth might just be 'getting more players,' not a portfolio finding.
articles.honest_critique: Elegant framing. Could be one mechanism dressed as two.

articles.what_is_missing: Context. Beane at $9M/trade in Oakland and Cashman at $6.34M in New York aren't doing the same job; the leaderboard pretends they are.
articles.honest_critique: The article's own methodology callout admits the GM name is shorthand for an entire org. Within-GM persistence is r=0.27 with a CI crossing zero — that's the buried headline. Ranking Coppolella as worst when his tenure ended in a signing-scandal void is measuring punishment, not skill.

cross_article_observations: Human variables entirely absent — no-trade clauses, agent leverage (Boras vs not), clubhouse/positional fit, makeup, family situation. Five articles, zero quotes from anyone who's been in a war room.
Coaching and staff continuity is a covariate that drives much of what gets attributed to GM and org.
Publishing findings while admitting central confounds are unrun is a pattern across multiple pieces.
what_i_actually_want_to_read_next: Coaching/staff continuity as a covariate — pitching coach, hitting coordinator, Latin American academy director impact on acquired-player outcomes.
Sell-side identity in the K-trajectory finding — who is selling Q4 pitchers and is it a concentrated list of orgs?
Trade outcomes conditional on no-trade-clause invocation and agent representation.
things_a_scout_would_tell_the_authors_ar: Human variables: NTCs, agents, clubhouse fit, makeup, family situation
